main_text.p: Voluptas belluarum est, igitur non hominis: reliqua vero partim suis adjunctis, partim causa efficienti procreante & conservante per adversa: Sunt enim caduca & incerta, posita non in nostris consiliis, sed in fortunæ temeritate. Qui autem Antapodo-sis, qua amicitia omnibus rebus humanis anteponitur: utpote quæ in virtute posita sit: nam eam hoc loco amicitiæ causam procreantem & conservantem constituit. Iam virtutem. Relabitur ad popularem & communem, quam suprapofuit, virtutis & boni viri descriptionem: virtus siquidem & bonus vir relativa sunt, & se mutuo constituunt. Tales igitur inter. Commendatio amicitiæ ab effectis, cujus propositio generalis est: Sine amicitia vita vitalis esse non potest: prima ejus ratio sumitur a testimonio Ennij Poetæ: altera a distributione vitæ humanæ e subjectis: quæ consistit vel in consiliis & sermonibus communicandis, vel in rebus ipsis administrandis: quæ rursus distribuuntur ex adjuncto in secundas & adversas: illas autem amicitia splendidiores facit, has vero faciliores. Deniq; cæteræ res.

page.notes: The page number at the head is printed in a long-s style ("3ʒ"); read as 33 with a doubt. Italic and roman runs are approximate where the scan is faint, notably "cæteræ" and the roman words "Qui autem", "Iam virtutem" and "Tales igitur inter". The word "Antapodo-sis" is hyphenated at the line end as printed. The last line of the page is a catchword-like phrase ending the text without a full stop; it is kept as printed.
